title: Robot Framework + Appium Mobile Test Generation Workflow

platform.description: Target mobile platform. android → UiAutomator2. ios → XCUITest.

execution_target.description: Where the Appium session runs. local — a local Appium server driving an Android Studio emulator/AVD, a physical device, or an iOS simulator. browserstack — BrowserStack App Automate cloud device farm (session opens against the BrowserStack hub with bstack:options capabilities).

appium_server_url.description: Base URL of the Appium endpoint. For execution_target=local this is the local Appium server (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4723). For execution_target=browserstack it is ignored in favour of browserstack.hub_url.

avd.description: Android Studio AVD (emulator) name to auto-launch via Appium (Appium 'avd' capability, e.g. Pixel_8_API_34). Only used when execution_target=local and platform=android. Optional — omit when the emulator/device is already running.

browserstack.description: BrowserStack App Automate settings. Required when execution_target=browserstack. Credentials are read from BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME / BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY env vars when username/access_key are null.

username.description: BrowserStack username. SECURITY: prefer leaving null and supplying BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME via env var.

access_key.description: BrowserStack access key. SECURITY: prefer leaving null and supplying BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY via env var. Never commit.

app_id.description: BrowserStack-hosted app identifier (bs://<hash>) returned by the app-upload REST API. Use this or app_path_upload.

app_path_upload.description: Local path to a .apk/.ipa to upload to BrowserStack before the run (via the app-upload REST API), producing a bs:// app_id. Use this or app_id.

device_name.description: Target device / emulator / simulator name (e.g. emulator-5554, iPhone 15). Written to .env as DEVICE_NAME.

platform_version.description: OS version of the target device (e.g. 14 for Android, 17.4 for iOS).

automation_name.description: Appium automation engine. Defaults to UiAutomator2 (Android) / XCUITest (iOS) when null.

app_package.description: Android application package id (e.g. com.everi.loyalty.kiosk). Required for android unless app_path is supplied.

app_activity.description: Android launch activity (e.g. .MainActivity). Optional when app_package is set.

bundle_id.description: iOS bundle identifier (e.g. com.everi.loyalty.kiosk). Required for ios unless app_path is supplied.

app_path.description: Path or URL to the app binary (.apk for Android, .app/.ipa for iOS). Used to install the app before the session.

app_version.description: Semver of the app build under test (e.g. 2.5.0). Exposed to tests via APP_VERSION / ${APP_VERSION}; drives version-scoped locator resolution.

app_username.description: In-app login username. Used when app_auth_strategy is env-var. Preflight writes this to .env. Never commit — keep workflow-input.current.json gitignored.

app_password.description: In-app login password. Used when app_auth_strategy is env-var. Preflight writes this to .env. Never commit.

app_auth_strategy.description: How the agent authenticates before analysing protected screens. none — app requires no login. env-var — log in with APP_USERNAME / APP_PASSWORD.

test_output_path.description: Folder (under the project root) where Robot Framework POM files are written. Overridden by the layout detected in an existing robot.yaml / project when a structure is found (Step 0).

report_output_path.description: Folder where Robot Framework output.xml / log.html / report.html are written after execution; ignored when robot_project_mode is existing.

screenshot_mode.description: all — Capture Page Screenshot after every step. on-failure — AppiumLibrary captures a screenshot only on failure (default). none — no screenshots.

log_level.description: step — Log at start/end of each test step. action — Log inside every page-object keyword as well. none — no generated logging.

robot_project_mode.description: new — generate robot.yaml / requirements.txt as part of the PR. existing — target repo already has a Robot Framework project; skip config generation and read the layout from the existing project.

robot_config_path.description: Relative path to robot.yaml (or the tests root) inside target_repo. Required when robot_project_mode is existing.

input_source.description: ado — fetch story title and test cases from Azure DevOps. raw-file — read test scenarios from a local file (markdown, plain text, or JSON); no ADO fetch in Phase 1.

raw_input_file.description: Path to the raw input file containing test scenarios. Required when input_source is raw-file. Supports .md, .txt, .json, and a Test Cases workflow output (.xlsx / testcase-generator .json, auto-converted via testcase-excel-to-rawinput). Path is relative to the workspace root.

user_story_ado_link.description: Full ADO URL for the user story work item. Use this or user_story_id when input_source is ado.

user_story_id.description: Numeric ADO work item ID for the user story (e.g. 1326051).

test_cases_ado_link.description: Full ADO test plan/suite URL. Use this or the test_plan_id + test_suite_id pair when input_source is ado.

target_local_path.description: OPTIONAL OVERRIDE. The .github folder always lives inside the target project, so the project root is auto-derived as the repository/workspace root that contains .github; generated files are written DIRECTLY there by default (resources/ and tests/ under the detected test_output_path, and in 'new' mode robot.yaml at the project root). The local project is the primary output target; mobile/artifacts/ retains a mirror copy only. Runs in both dry-run and execute modes and is independent of ADO PR creation. Set this only to point at a DIFFERENT directory.

spec_name_override.description: Override the .robot suite file name (kebab-case, without .robot); defaults to the story title.

target_screens.description: Screen names / feature areas to restrict analysis to (e.g. ['Login', 'Dashboard']); empty means analyse all reachable screens derived from the scenarios.

ado_pat.description: Azure DevOps Personal Access Token. SECURITY: do NOT store the token here — keep this null and supply it via the ADO_PAT environment variable, which preflight reads as a fallback. Required (via env var or this field) when input_source is ado or run_mode is execute.

ado_project.description: Azure DevOps project name (e.g. Loyalty Kiosk).

self_healing.description: Optional locator self-healing stage. When omitted, null, or enabled=false, the orchestrator skips heal-tests.agent.md. When enabled, consumes a Robot Framework output.xml, isolates locator-driven failures, and repairs only resources/locators/*.resource files by re-inspecting the live app via Appium before PR creation.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false, the entire self_healing object is ignored and the heal stage is skipped.

heal_task.description: heal-failures — repair broken locators from a test run. validate-version — verify locators against an upgraded app version and preserve per-version selectors. audit — read-only health check of all locators (reports ok/broken/skipped, writes nothing).

app_version.description: Semver of the app currently under test (e.g. 2.5.0). Required when heal_task is validate-version. Exposed to tests via APP_VERSION / ${APP_VERSION}.

previous_app_version.description: Last known-good semver whose selectors must remain valid (e.g. 2.4.3). Required when heal_task is validate-version.

heal_mode.description: report-driven — consume an existing Robot Framework output.xml (agent does not execute tests); returns a re-run command. agent-run — the agent executes the suite itself.

results_report_path.description: Path to the Robot Framework output.xml produced by your run (report-driven mode). Generate with: robot --outputdir results mobile-tests/tests

max_attempts_per_locator.description: Maximum re-inspection attempts per broken locator before reverting and flagging for manual verification.

max_total_reruns.description: Cap on full/partial suite re-executions across the whole healing loop (agent-run mode only).

heal_shared_locators.description: When true, resources/locators/shared-components.locators.resource may be healed in addition to per-screen locator files.

strategy.description: accessibility-first — prefer accessibility_id / content-desc / label before id/xpath. id-first — prefer resource-id / name, then accessibility, then xpath.
